questions.domain: Service Desk Foundations and User Experience
questions.prompt: Explain service desk purpose in Service Desk Foundations and User Experience. Which user or service outcome should it protect?
questions.preferred_answer: The service desk is the central point of contact that connects users with the service provider and restores access to value. A strong response connects the concept to the support outcome, then explains that the operator should capture context, communicate clearly, own or coordinate the case, and confirm the user outcome. Evidence should include user impact, contact history, agreed next update and closure confirmation. It should explicitly avoid treating the desk as a ticket-routing queue rather than a relationship and recovery function.
evaluation_points: capture context, communicate clearly, own or coordinate the case, and confirm the user outcome
user impact, contact history, agreed next update and closure confirmation
Recognises risk: treating the desk as a ticket-routing queue rather than a relationship and recovery function

questions.domain: Service Desk Foundations and User Experience
questions.prompt: How would you apply service desk purpose consistently during day-to-day support without turning it into a checkbox?
questions.preferred_answer: Start from the actual user and service outcome described in the case. Then capture context, communicate clearly, own or coordinate the case, and confirm the user outcome. Keep a decision trail using user impact, contact history, agreed next update and closure confirmation, review exceptions, and confirm the result with the affected user or service owner. The process fails when it becomes treating the desk as a ticket-routing queue rather than a relationship and recovery function.
evaluation_points: capture context, communicate clearly, own or coordinate the case, and confirm the user outcome
Avoids treating the desk as a ticket-routing queue rather than a relationship and recovery function

questions.domain: Service Desk Foundations and User Experience
questions.prompt: What is incident versus service request, and what evidence would help you recognise it correctly in a live support case?
questions.preferred_answer: An incident is an unplanned interruption or reduction in quality; a service request is a predefined user need such as access, information or a standard fulfilment. Recognition should not rely on the ticket label alone. The analyst should collect symptoms, affected service, catalogue item, entitlement and workflow history, compare the observation with the expected service state, and then classify by outcome, apply the correct workflow and avoid hiding failures inside request queues. A key error is misclassification distorting SLA, prioritisation and problem data.
evaluation_points: symptoms, affected service, catalogue item, entitlement and workflow history
Distinguishes from misclassification distorting SLA, prioritisation and problem data

questions.domain: Service Desk Foundations and User Experience
questions.prompt: A case involving incident versus service request is repeatedly reopened. Give an evidence-led troubleshooting and escalation sequence.
questions.preferred_answer: Restate the user-visible failure and establish scope. Collect symptoms, affected service, catalogue item, entitlement and workflow history; review previous actions and recent changes; form a small number of testable hypotheses; then classify by outcome, apply the correct workflow and avoid hiding failures inside request queues. Preserve a known-good rollback and escalate with the chronology and a precise specialist ask. Do not repeat misclassification distorting SLA, prioritisation and problem data.
evaluation_points: symptoms, affected service, catalogue item, entitlement and workflow history
Avoids misclassification distorting SLA, prioritisation and problem data

questions.prompt: Design a support workflow or control for user-centred communication that can operate across a large endpoint estate.
questions.preferred_answer: The design objective is: Support communication translates technical uncertainty into clear expectations while preserving dignity and trust. Define ownership, entry criteria, standard actions and exception paths. The workflow should use plain language, verify understanding, set update times and adapt to the user context; retain repeated-back understanding, written recap, consent and sentiment; pilot on a representative cohort; and include rollback, audit and user communication. It must be designed against technical accuracy without usable communication or unsupported promises.
evaluation_points: use plain language, verify understanding, set update times and adapt to the user context
repeated-back understanding, written recap, consent and sentiment

questions.prompt: What are the main trade-offs and failure modes when scaling user-centred communication, and how would you evaluate control effectiveness?

At scale, the major failure mode is technical accuracy without usable communication or unsupported promises. Evaluate both coverage and outcome: verify repeated-back understanding, written recap, consent and sentiment, sample real cases, inspect exceptions and user impact, and confirm that teams actually use plain language, verify understanding, set update times and adapt to the user context. A high completion count is not proof of an effective control.

questions.prompt: How should an organisation govern end-to-end ownership across regions, vendors and support tiers?
questions.preferred_answer: Governance should define the outcome (Ownership means remaining accountable for progress and communication even when another team performs the technical work.), accountable owner, minimum evidence, role boundaries, privacy/security requirements, exception authority and review cycle. Operational teams should coordinate handoffs, maintain updates, challenge stalled queues and validate restoration and retain assignment trail, update cadence, dependency owner and user confirmation. Quality assurance should sample cases and look specifically for ticket ping-pong and silent transfers.

questions.domain: Service Desk Foundations and User Experience
questions.prompt: A senior user asks the service desk to bypass normal controls to resolve an urgent issue involving end-to-end ownership. What do you do?
questions.preferred_answer: Acknowledge urgency but do not equate seniority with authorisation. Establish the business impact and minimum safe outcome: Ownership means remaining accountable for progress and communication even when another team performs the technical work. Collect assignment trail, update cadence, dependency owner and user confirmation; choose the lowest-risk reversible action; and coordinate handoffs, maintain updates, challenge stalled queues and validate restoration. If an exception is still required, obtain the authorised owner, scope, expiry, monitoring and rollback. Refuse or escalate any request that would create ticket ping-pong and silent transfers.
